A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChatBench study and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained results and relocated appendix material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Prolific user-study results, AI-alone experiments, conversation analyses, and user-simulator experiments in Sections 3–5 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds participant-demographic comparisons and further conversation statistics.

M1.justification: The benchmark-to-conversation study procedure, free-text AI-alone method, and two-step simulator training and inference remain unchanged. The revised annotation prompt concerns post-hoc conversation analysis, rather than the proposed simulator.

E1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly uses U.S. Census population data and BLS employment statistics to assess participant representativeness. This adds ancillary demographic comparison data; the 396 MMLU questions, five subjects, recruited population, and answer-first/direct-to-AI tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same AI-alone variants, IQA-EVAL, and unfine-tuned Two-Step simulator. GPT-4o-mini also remains in the retained pilot comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Listing 5 replaces the broader annotation questionnaire with four specified outputs, and benchmark-mirroring now requires a single AI answer. Appendix B.3 changes the correction criterion from the last to the first AI answer, although Figure B1's caption still says last. Main study and simulator settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Supplementary analyses expand substantially through a demographic representativeness audit (Figure A1) and conversation diagnostics covering message length, prompt types, answer provision, and user responses (Table B1). The error/correction analysis is also revised. Existing pilot, confidence, and simulator analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 AI-alone answers per question, 10 simulator conversations per test question, 100 correlation-bound simulation iterations, and the same standard-error and z-test procedures. The added descriptive statistics introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Section 4.3 substantially revises conversation findings: benchmark-mirroring changes from 34% to 39.8%, and GPT-4o's correct/no-clear-answer/wrong breakdown in the error cases changes from 36/43/21% to 26/67/7%. Llama estimates and Figure B1 also change, while Figure A1 and Table B1 add results. These accompany revised analysis rules; Tables 1 and A1–A3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 retains the same statistical formulas and binomial simulation argument for the correlation upper bound. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: ChatBench connects static and interactive evaluation, AI-alone accuracy poorly predicts user-AI accuracy, and fine-tuning improves user-simulator agreement with human data.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies demographic non-representativeness, explains why short conversations can still contain meaningful interaction, and interprets Moral Scenarios as showing greater user independence. It also softens the correction interpretation, describing corrections as uncommon and removing the explicit claim that they explain the narrowing model-performance gap.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies React and Azure CosmosDB, documents demographic sources and category filtering/normalization, and specifies revised annotation outputs in Listing 5. Simulator hyperparameters, code and dataset access information, and privacy/filtering procedures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ipeirotis (2010), Posch et al. (2022), and Census/BLS sources for the demographic analysis. It also uses the existing WildChat reference to contextualize short conversations. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix A is reorganized into Task Details, Pilots and Incentivization, and ChatBench, with interface discussion moved into Task Details. Conversation-analysis prose is revised and expanded, alongside small introduction and acknowledgment edits. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the demographic Figure A1 and conversation Table B1, redraws Figures 5 and B1, and changes B1's vertical scale. The pilot figure becomes A2, and confidence/simulator figures are redistributed across appendix pages. Main comparison tables and interface screenshots are retained.

improvement.justification: The demographic audit and Table B1 make participant representativeness and interaction behavior easier to assess, while adding concrete qualifications about sampling. These provide a modest benefit with the central methods and performance evidence unchanged. The first-versus-last-answer contradiction between Appendix B.3 and Figure B1's caption introduces a localized clarity problem that limits the improvement.
